prompt: Call a method chosen at runtime by its name, passing arguments through reflection -- including a private one. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Method.invoke is the reflective equivalent of writing target.method(args), with two differences that trip people up: the return value always arrives as an Object (so an int comes back boxed), and a private method needs setAccessible(true) before it will run. Matching on name plus parameter count sidesteps the boxing mismatch between an Integer argument and an int parameter, which is the usual reason a getDeclaredMethod lookup fails. Throwing NoSuchMethodException when nothing matches keeps the failure explicit rather than returning null and hiding a typo.
hints: Loop over target.getClass().getDeclaredMethods() and test two things: method.getName().equals(methodName) and method.getParameterCount() == args.length.
Call method.setAccessible(true) before invoking -- shout is private and will otherwise throw IllegalAccessException.

Return method.invoke(target, args) directly: args is already an Object[], which is exactly what invoke's varargs parameter wants. Throw new NoSuchMethodException(methodName) only after the loop finds nothing.
